summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted with recurrent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and low-grade fever shortly after a prior discharge for similar symptoms. He has a complex history including HCV cirrhosis, hepatopulmonary syndrome on remodulin, and pancytopenia. On admission, he was started on IV antibiotics due to immunocompromise and concern for infection. Workup revealed no bacterial source; stool studies were negative, and imaging showed no evidence of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. A left lower lobe pneumonia was noted but remained asymptomatic. EGD and colonoscopy showed stable varices and portal gastropathy without acute pathology, and biopsies were non-diagnostic. His symptoms were attributed to medication effects (remodulin and doxycycline) and possible viral gastroenteritis. Doxycycline was discontinued per infectious disease. Pancytopenia was deemed chronic and due to splenic sequestration. He improved clinically, was weaned off IV antibiotics, and discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up in transplant clinic, where he was officially listed for liver transplantation.
